rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled"; i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), items 1 and 3; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person; i2441 p. 3, Line 2; i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative’s support, special rules may apply"; i1040gi p. 17, Step 1 (a qualifying child is tested on relationship, age, own support, joint return and residency; no support test of yours). The box test (dc_qp, dc_incapable, over 13 at year end, or 13 with dc_over12_care) is the project's. Inherits its dependent.dc_qp. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,463 comparisons): 6,431 of 7,463 agree; 511 candidate-refuses, 507 candidate-unknown, 13 value, 1 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 83 candidate-refuses, 49 candidate-unknown, 4 value. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/classify.py, none unassigned; the uncapped rerun reproduces the recorded counts exactly): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative); (b) 4 value, candidate checked and project not, all with f2441.care no (generated 35, 355, 401, 437), reaching no amount; (c) 30 candidate-unknown on returns with f2441.care no, where the reply asks dependent.dc_incapable, dc_under13 or dc_over12_care because it has no care-expense test (for example classm.aqee.2 k0, stage18.blind.p15 k0, generated 64); (d) 1 lawful fixture; (e) 18 partial records withholding an answer the reply needs (9 dc_incapable, 3 lawful, and single divorced_rule, married, months, multiple_support, other_claimant, relationship of classm.scveh.1). Project stands.

Two differences contradict the source. (1) Inherited from dc_qp: on stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (by reading; age 80, dc_incapable yes, a qualifying person under p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025") the project checks the box and the candidate does not. (2) The candidate omits f2441.care, so it checks column (c) for a disabled person over 12 on a return with no care and no Form 2441; i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled", and with no care there is no line 2 entry (round 2 ruled the same reading model error; class M classm.dependent.1 dep_b is this case). Representation: for a 13-year-old the candidate also checks the box when dc_under13 is no, which on consistent answers means every included expense was for care at 13 or older, the project's dc_over12_care yes. The joint-return route is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns)).

No full qualification or new numeric evidence is claimed.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: second transcription right in part; proposed finding (the box changes no amount). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled." The project checks the box for every qualifying person not able to care for themselves except a qualifying child under 13 all year (`dependent.dc_child_all_year` false), so a qualifying person under 13 who is not your qualifying child but qualifies through the disabled route (for example an unrelated child aged 10 who lived with you all year as a member of your household, your dependent as a qualifying relative, and not able to care for themselves) is checked though never over age 12; the second leaves it unchecked. Proposed fix: replace the `dependent.dc_child_all_year == false` test with the age, `dependent.age` not less than `dc.child_age` (13 or over at the end of 2025). The second also leaves the box unchecked for a disabled qualifying child who turned 13 in 2025 (its note); there the project is retained: care given after the 13th birthday was given while the child was over age 12 and disabled, and column (c) adds "A person over age 12 at the time the care was provided must be physically or mentally incapable of caring for themselves to be listed on line 2", which is that child's position for that care. Fixed during integration (BUG-0080): `dependent.dc_line2c` now tests the person's age against `dc.child_age` (13) instead of `dependent.dc_child_all_year`.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; numeric count literals in the returned h_lived_half (6) and the household-year test (12) omit type:Count. Untyped numbers are money cents in the declared IR, so comparing them with Count months yields unknown; the typed project comparison yields a Boolean. This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force. The model uses the direct care-timing question; the project infers older/younger ages and asks only at age13. The actual age-at-care correction is independently covered by render and the six boundary checks.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling; the box changes no amount). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): 'Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled.' The project checks it for a qualifying person who is not able to care for themselves and is 13 or older at the end of 2025; the second writes the qualifying-person test in its own structure. The one case the box could differ, a disabled child who turned 13 in 2025 and had care only before the birthday, is not asked and changes no amount.

After BUG-0080's fix the sides differ only for a disabled qualifying child who turned 13 during 2025: the project checks the box (age 13 or more at the end of 2025, unable to care for themselves), the second checks it only for a person not under 13 for any part of 2025. i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled"; the care after the birthday counts only through the disability rule (i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), "If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13"), so the person listed was over age 12 and disabled for that care. Listed for the owner as a display reading.

The one case the box could differ, a disabled child who turned 13 in 2025 and had care only before the birthday, is not asked and changes no amount.

The total is the same; the benefits reading is the register's (amb.2025.dc_line30).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. The candidate is "dc_paid if its own dc_qp (without f2441.care) holds, else 0", so it inherits dc_qp's missing death-year rule: on stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (by reading) the project shows $4,000 and the candidate $0, and p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Other differences: (a) for a person who is not a qualifying person the project shows dc_paid unconditionally, but the interview asks dc_paid only where Form 2441 sums the column (f2441 sums dependent.dc_line2d where dependent.dc_qp holds; the evaluator is lazy), so that is representation on producible records, i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s)"; (b) the joint-return route is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns)); (c) the candidate's note keeps benefits in column (d), which is the register's chosen reading (amb.2025.dc_line30).

This adjudicates placement of the row filter on eligible rows, not the returned dc_qp predicate, whose availability defect is ruled separately. The prior gross-column/net-line30 ambiguity amb.2025.dc_line30 remains recorded; no new owner choice is inferred.

The project copies the supplied expense amount in the entry and filters qualifying rows when Form2441 aggregates; the model adds a qualifying-person choose around the entry amount. This rules only on filter placement on eligible rows, not the correctness of the returned qualifying-person predicate (ruled separately). The existing gross-column/net-line30 presentation ambiguity amb.2025.dc_line30 remains recorded; it is not new owner approval.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The second zeroes column (d) for an entry that is not a qualifying person; the project shows the entry's expenses and the line 3 total `f2441.paid_total` sums column (d) only over the dependents with `dependent.dc_qp` true, so no amount on the form differs (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s)"). The second's note leaves the Part III benefits to lines 29 to 31, which is the binding reading `amb.2025.dc_line30` (column (d) before excluding benefits; i2441 p. 3, Column (d), "If you completed Part III, don't include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28"); 2024 expenses paid in 2025 are refused on line 9b (`f2441.prior_year`), which the project's column (d) need not read since the input excludes them ("Do not include 2024 care paid in 2025"; i2441 p. 3, Column (d), "Expenses you incurred in 2024 but didn't pay until 2025. Instead, see the instructions for line 9b").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project copies the person's qualified expenses and applies the qualifying-person test where column (d) is summed (f2441.paid_total, 'where dependent.dc_qp'); the second zeroes the column for a person who is not a qualifying person (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s), earlier"). By reading, the reply's eligible-student test (dependent.h_edu_student: claimed, edu, edu_1098t, the student's tin) no longer has the filer-TIN test it had last round, so a return whose filer has no TIN keeps the American opportunity credit where the project moves the student to line 31. No sampled record has that combination; a constructed witness, stage19.example.jack_kay (joint return, student k0) with person[spouse].tin no and itin_applied no, evaluated with both sides (scratch /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/cand_eval.py): project line 27 $0.00 (hidden), line 30 $0.00, line 31 $4,300.00, Form 8863 line 19 $860.00, f1040 line 24 $3,286.00; reply line 27 $4,000.00, line 30 $2,500.00, line 31 $0.00, line 19 $1,500.00, line 24 $2,646.00. It also has no f8863.paid test, so it asks dependent.edu where no qualified education expenses were paid. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,463 comparisons): 3,871 of 7,463 agree; 3,080 candidate-unknown, 508 candidate-refuses, 3 project-refuses, 1 project-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 1,076 candidate-unknown, 83 candidate-refuses. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/classify.py, none unassigned): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4 withholding an unrelated answer); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative) (the project hides the line); (b) 1,059 candidate-unknown dependent.edu on records with f8863.paid no, where the project hides the line: an answer the source does not need; (c) 3 candidate-unknown dependent.lawful on fixtures that predate the question for a household_member (classm.clcw26.2 and .deepseek dep_b, stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn all_year): an extra question with no amount, since the household_member answer already states the local-law condition; (d) 14 candidate-unknown, partials withholding multiple_support of a qualifying child. No value difference on the sample. Project stands.

Witness: generated 99 (the taxpayer has no TIN; the round-2 generated 47, renumbered by the generator change): the project sends dep_a and dep_b to line 31 ($12,706.94 and $5,509.61) and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate keeps them on lines 27 to 30 and shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped) and $0.00 on line 31, against the quoted item 5. Line 28 is the aqee line28 of its line 27 (the source's "Subtract $2,000 from line 27"). The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)), and inlines its own dependent.claimed (household_member without the all-year test, multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 47 (the taxpayer has no TIN): the project sends dep_a to line 31 and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped), against the quoted item 5. No value differs this round: the reply now counts other with the lawful answer. Line 28 reads the candidate's line 27 (its line 28 is the source's "Subtract $2,000 from line 27"). The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu_over, which its note makes a refusal); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its own edu_over refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses; project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 36, 265, 285, 409, 454), the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen. Its edu_over refusal reads the reworded question (BUG-0197) as the project does. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); it now reads the project's aqee definition for the arithmetic and its own dependent.claimed (multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 99 (the taxpayer has no TIN; the round-2 generated 47, renumbered by the generator change): the project sends dep_a and dep_b to line 31 ($12,706.94 and $5,509.61) and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate keeps them on lines 27 to 30 and shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped) and $0.00 on line 31, against the quoted item 5. Line 29 is the aqee line29 (25% of its line 28). The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu); its refusals are its own edu_over gate on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses, and its multiple_support placement (classm.s3.4.deepseek without dependent.edu, completed). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)), and inlines its own dependent.claimed (household_member without the all-year test, multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 47 (the taxpayer has no TIN): the project sends dep_a to line 31 and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped), against the quoted item 5. No value differs this round: the reply now counts other with the lawful answer. Line 29 reads the candidate's line 28 (its line 28 is the source's "Subtract $2,000 from line 27"). The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu_over, which its note makes a refusal); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its own edu_over refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses; project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 36, 265, 285, 409, 454), the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen. Its edu_over refusal reads the reworded question (BUG-0197) as the project does. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)) and inlines its own dependent.claimed, which drops the other relationship. Witnesses: generated 47 (the taxpayer has no TIN, household.tin_count 0): the project sends dep_a to line 31 and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped) and its AOC chain, against the quoted item 5; classm.s3.2 and classm.s3.2.deepseek dep_a and generated 145 dep_b (relationship other, 12 months, completed): the project claims the dependent and gives $4,000.00 / $2,416.87 on line 27, the candidate $0.00, its dependent.claimed error. The 4,094 candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where dependent.edu is not asked (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5). Project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen (generated 36, 146, 265, 285, 409, 454); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its D3 refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); it now reads the project's aqee definition for the arithmetic and its own dependent.claimed (multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 99 (the taxpayer has no TIN; the round-2 generated 47, renumbered by the generator change): the project sends dep_a and dep_b to line 31 ($12,706.94 and $5,509.61) and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate keeps them on lines 27 to 30 and shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped) and $0.00 on line 31, against the quoted item 5. Line 30 is the aqee line30 ("If line 28 is zero, enter the amount from line 27. Otherwise, add $2,000 to the amount on line 29"). The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu); its refusals are its own edu_over gate on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses, and its multiple_support placement (classm.s3.4.deepseek without dependent.edu, completed). Its edu_over gate omits the project's "edu_adj above zero", which a Yes to the reworded question implies (assistance above a period's expenses is above zero). The project-refuses are its cited screens on refused returns: dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 111, 250, 285; i1040gi p. 22), dependent.married (generated 23; i1040gi p. 21), dependent.other_claimant (generated 75) and dependent.divorced_rule (generated 210): scope. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)), and inlines its own dependent.claimed (household_member without the all-year test, multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 47 (the taxpayer has no TIN): the project sends dep_a to line 31 and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped), against the quoted item 5. No value differs this round: the reply now counts other with the lawful answer. Line 30 reads the candidate's line 29 (its line 28 is the source's "Subtract $2,000 from line 27"). The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu_over, which its note makes a refusal); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its own edu_over refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses; project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 36, 265, 285, 409, 454), the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen. Its edu_over refusal reads the reworded question (BUG-0197) as the project does. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)) and inlines its own dependent.claimed, which drops the other relationship. Witnesses: generated 47 (the taxpayer has no TIN, household.tin_count 0): the project sends dep_a to line 31 and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate shows $4,000.00 on line 27 (candidate-shows-skipped) and its AOC chain, against the quoted item 5; classm.s3.2 and classm.s3.2.deepseek dep_a and generated 145 dep_b (relationship other, 12 months, completed): the project claims the dependent and gives $4,000.00 / $2,416.87 on line 27, the candidate $0.00, its dependent.claimed error. The 4,094 candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where dependent.edu is not asked (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5). Project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen (generated 36, 146, 265, 285, 409, 454); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its D3 refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 2, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student"; i8863 p. 3, item 5: "Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)" (amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, reading 1: both spouses on a joint return); i8863 p. 9, Line 31. By reading, the reply's eligible-student test (dependent.h_edu_student: claimed, edu, edu_1098t, the student's tin) no longer has the filer-TIN test it had last round, so a return whose filer has no TIN keeps the American opportunity credit where the project moves the student to line 31. No sampled record has that combination; a constructed witness, stage19.example.jack_kay (joint return, student k0) with person[spouse].tin no and itin_applied no, evaluated with both sides (scratch /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/cand_eval.py): project line 27 $0.00 (hidden), line 30 $0.00, line 31 $4,300.00, Form 8863 line 19 $860.00, f1040 line 24 $3,286.00; reply line 27 $4,000.00, line 30 $2,500.00, line 31 $0.00, line 19 $1,500.00, line 24 $2,646.00. It also has no f8863.paid test, so it asks dependent.edu where no qualified education expenses were paid. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,463 comparisons): 3,869 of 7,463 agree; 3,082 candidate-unknown, 508 candidate-refuses, 3 project-refuses, 1 project-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 1,076 candidate-unknown, 83 candidate-refuses. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr3-dependent/classify.py, none unassigned): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4 withholding an unrelated answer); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative) (the project hides the line); (b) 1,059 candidate-unknown dependent.edu on records with f8863.paid no, where the project hides the line: an answer the source does not need; (c) 3 candidate-unknown dependent.lawful on fixtures that predate the question for a household_member (classm.clcw26.2 and .deepseek dep_b, stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn all_year): an extra question with no amount, since the household_member answer already states the local-law condition; (d) 14 candidate-unknown, partials withholding multiple_support of a qualifying child. No value difference on the sample. Project stands.

The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); it now reads the project's aqee definition for the arithmetic and its own dependent.claimed (multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 99 (the taxpayer has no TIN; the round-2 generated 47, renumbered by the generator change): the project sends dep_a and dep_b to line 31 ($12,706.94 and $5,509.61) and hides lines 27 to 30; the candidate keeps them on lines 27 to 30 and shows $0.00 here (the two values), against the quoted item 5. The amount (institution-paid expenses less lines 2a to 2c, floored at zero) is the project's aqee ws4_llc. The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu); its refusals are its own edu_over gate on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses, and its multiple_support placement (classm.s3.4.deepseek without dependent.edu, completed). Its edu_over gate omits the project's "edu_adj above zero", which a Yes to the reworded question implies (assistance above a period's expenses is above zero). The project-refuses are its cited screens on refused returns: dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 111, 250, 285; i1040gi p. 22), dependent.married (generated 23; i1040gi p. 21), dependent.other_claimant (generated 75) and dependent.divorced_rule (generated 210): scope. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." As last round the candidate omits f8863.paid and the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)), and inlines its own dependent.claimed (household_member without the all-year test, multiple support refused for a child). Witness: generated 47 (filer without a TIN): the project sends the student to line 31 ($14,396.61) where the candidate, lacking the filer-TIN test, keeps the student on lines 27 to 30 and shows $0.00 here. The amount (institution-paid expenses less lines 2a to 2c, floored at zero) is the project's aqee ws4_llc. The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the dependent's education answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5: the candidate needs dependent.edu_over, which its note makes a refusal); candidate refusals are its multiple_support and married placements (classm.s3.4, classm.f8880.4) and its own edu_over refusal on stage19.refuse.period_over_dependent, which the project also refuses; project refusals are dependent.claimed_no_tin (generated 36, 265, 285, 409, 454), the cited i1040gi p. 22 screen. Its edu_over refusal reads the reworded question (BUG-0197) as the project does. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,284 partial records): 3,186 of 6,903 comparisons agree; 152 candidate-refuses, 3,559 candidate-unknown, 5 project-refuses, 1 value; on returns the full interview completes: 2 candidate-refuses, 1,209 candidate-unknown.

Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 6,535 agree; 101 candidate-refuses (47 completed), 26 candidate-unknown, 111 project-unknown, 1 value. The candidate's Step 3 test is the project's; every difference comes from its dependent.claimed: the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records of classm.f2441.1.deepseek and classm.f2441.5.deepseek): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"; household.credit_disallowed, which it adds as a refusal, is refused by the project on Schedule 8812 on the same returns. The one value (classm.sc.2 dep_b, a refused return) is the joint-return route with sa.dependent yes: Step 2 q. 3 lets a joint filer skip q. 4, but sa.dependent yes is refused at Form 1040 line 12e (sa.standard), as ruled in rounds 2 and 3: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding married, other_claimant or divorced_rule, which the interview asks of every listed person (the refusal gates of dependent.qualifying_child). Project stands.

This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative’s support, special rules may apply"; i1040gi p. 17, Step 1 (a qualifying child is tested on relationship, age, own support, joint return and residency; no support test of yours). The reply still declares dependent.multiple_support on dependent.claimed itself, so it refuses a qualifying child whose support was shared. Compared with its round-3 reply, the reply restores the Form 2441 death-year route (stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year now agrees: dc_qp yes, dc_count 1, line 2(d) $4,000.00, line 11 $600.00 on both sides) and adds the born, died and placed route to its qualifying-child residency test (dependent.h_residency). executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,463 comparisons): 6,650 of 7,463 agree; 317 project-refuses, 279 candidate-unknown, 117 candidate-refuses, 99 project-unknown, 1 value; on returns the full interview completes: 83 candidate-refuses, 29 candidate-unknown. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/classify.py, none unassigned; the uncapped rerun reproduces the recorded counts exactly): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative); (b) 3 candidate-unknown dependent.lawful on fixtures whose household_member entries predate that question (classm.clcw26.2 and .deepseek dep_b, stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn all_year); (c) 6 candidate-unknown dependent.born_died: the reply's dependent.h_residency asks it of every person with months under 7, but dependent.months already folds in the birth, death and placement exception ("For a person born, died, adopted or placed with you in 2025 who meets the other conditions to be your qualifying child, enter 12 if your home was their home for more than half the time they were alive or with you"; i1040gi p. 21, Exception to time lived with you), so the interview never asks it there (classm.f8960.2 and .deepseek dep_a, audit.dependent.listed_not_dependent_no_tin child, generated 64, 100, 405); an answer the source does not need; (d) 20 partial records withholding an answer the reply needs first (19 multiple_support, 1 divorced_rule). Off completed returns, the 317 project-refuses are its cited dependent screens (claimed_no_tin and those of dependent.qualifying_child) on returns refused anyway. BUG-0258 rewords dependent.parent_home_paid only; this line does not read it. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household if your relationship didn't violate local law"; p501 p. 19, Local law violated: "A person doesn't meet this test if at any time during the year the relationship between you and that person violates local law." Finding L1 (new, low): the candidate applies the local-law condition to sibling_descendant as well as other, and that is the source's reading. A sibling_descendant (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child) is none of the relatives Step 4 lists ("Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them"), so it qualifies only under the quoted bullet; dependent.qr_relationship requires dependent.lawful only for other (the test "relationship ne other OR lawful"), so the interview never asks it for a sibling_descendant who lived with you all year. Constructed witness, executed (node engine/dist/main.js eval, /tmp/adj-s19r2-pd/w_sibdesc.json, classm.s3.2 with dep_a sibling_descendant aged 30): dependent.claimed yes, odc_amount $500.00, f1040 line 19 $1,000.00; the same entry as other with lawful no gives claimed no, $0.00 and $500.00. No triage record has a sibling_descendant all-year entry (the generator draws none). The reply now has the local-law test for other (lawful, 12 months), as the project. Its own differences: (a) it counts household_member with no all-year test, trusting the relationship label against the months answer (classm.tcw.5 dep_a, completed: household_member, months 2, project no, candidate yes; classm.dependent.4 and classm.dependent.4.deepseek dep_c, months 11; generated 118 and 129): the quoted bullet requires "lived with you all year", which the project tests as months 12; (b) it refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed; generated 126, 186, 243), against i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"; (c) its joint-return exception to sa.dependent (mfj) differs only on returns the project refuses at sa.standard (classm.sc.2 dep_b): scope on that kind. The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2, classm.ltc.2, classm.s1.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20; classm.sc.1), all on refused returns: scope. The project-unknown are partials withholding tin or months, which the interview asks of every listed person. The reply's Step 3 tests (the child's TIN, citizenship, age under 17, SSN valid for employment, and household.ctc_ssn) are the project's. Every difference comes from its inlined dependent.claimed: the multiple_support refusal for a qualifying child (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, completed; classm.asset.1, classm.gift.1, classm.qdcg.3, classm.tcw.3 on refused returns) and the same answer needed where a partial withholds it (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f2441.5.deepseek, classm.sd.1.deepseek without multiple_support); The rise in completed-return candidate-refuses (2 last round, 83 now) is the bank, not the reply: the reply refused dependent.multiple_support on every entry last round too, and the regenerated bank (1,323 fixtures, partial bases every fourth reached fixture) now draws partial records from returns carrying the classm.s3.4 child (inferred from the witnesses; triage records only six per kind). rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

Every difference comes from its inlined dependent.claimed: the multiple_support refusal for a qualifying child (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, completed; classm.asset.1, classm.gift.1, classm.qdcg.3, classm.tcw.3 on refused returns) and the same answer needed where a partial withholds it (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f2441.5.deepseek, classm.sd.1.deepseek without multiple_support); The rise in completed-return candidate-refuses (2 last round, 83 now) is the bank, not the reply: the reply refused dependent.multiple_support on every entry last round too, and the regenerated bank (1,323 fixtures, partial bases every fourth reached fixture) now draws partial records from returns carrying the classm.s3.4 child (inferred from the witnesses; triage records only six per kind). The one value is classm.sc.2 dep_b, where its joint-return exception to sa.dependent applies on a return the project refuses at sa.standard ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35): scope on that kind. Project-unknown records are partials withholding married, other_claimant or divorced_rule, which the project asks first (classm.f8889.4.deepseek, classm.f8960.1.deepseek). Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.json; 1,323 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,268 partial records): 6,622 of 6,899 comparisons agree; 157 candidate-refuses, 20 candidate-unknown, 99 project-unknown, 1 value; on returns the full interview completes: 83 candidate-refuses, 15 candidate-unknown.

The returned helpers explicitly defer those facts to callers and omit the available sa.dependent/household interfaces; the requested per-person exported credit results therefore do not implement those prerequisites. Passing expression types does not establish source agreement. The now-complete relationship descriptions and typed Count thresholds fix the previous request/IR defects, but do not fix this omission. No project tax change or new numeric evidence is inferred.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. After normalizing nesting, the only difference from the project is that the candidate replaces "sa.dependent is no" by "f1040.status is mfj or sa.dependent is no". The candidate follows the source, i1040gi p. 18, Step 2: "3. Are you filing a joint return for 2025? Yes. You can claim this child as a dependent", asked before question 4 ("Could you be claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return?"); i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, question 4 is the same for a qualifying relative. The project tests sa.dependent alone, but the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns). Latent only: lifting the sa.dependent screen needs Step 2 question 3 and Step 4 question 4 in qc_dependent and qr_dependent.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 18, Step 3 asks of a qualifying child "Does Your Qualifying Child Qualify You for the Child Tax Credit" (questions 1-4: SSN, ITIN or ATIN; citizen, national or resident alien; under 17; SSN valid for employment). Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 6,535 agree; 101 candidate-refuses (47 completed), 26 candidate-unknown, 111 project-unknown, 1 value. The candidate's Step 3 test is the project's; every difference comes from its dependent.claimed: the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records of classm.f2441.1.deepseek and classm.f2441.5.deepseek): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"; household.credit_disallowed, which it adds as a refusal, is refused by the project on Schedule 8812 on the same returns. The one value (classm.sc.2 dep_b, a refused return) is the joint-return route with sa.dependent yes: Step 2 q. 3 lets a joint filer skip q. 4, but sa.dependent yes is refused at Form 1040 line 12e (sa.standard), as ruled in rounds 2 and 3: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding married, other_claimant or divorced_rule, which the interview asks of every listed person (the refusal gates of dependent.qualifying_child). Project stands.

The second gives 1 for a qualifying person and 0 otherwise; the project's per-entry count is 1 and the only line that reads it, `f2441.qp_count`, sums it over the dependents with `dependent.dc_qp` true, so the number of qualifying persons is the same (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Complete columns (a) through (d) for each qualifying person" and "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s), earlier").

The total is the same.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s): "1. A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent ... 3. Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person. The reply's disabled route now applies the death-year rule (dependent.h_half_dc: months over 6, or born_died with part_year_home), so the previous round's stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year value no longer differs; it omits "you have care expenses", which its own column (d) applies through dependent.h_dc_counts. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,382 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,447 comparisons): 4,483 of 7,447 agree; 1,647 value, 794 candidate-unknown, 510 candidate-refuses, 12 project-unknown, 1 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 702 value, 84 candidate-unknown, 83 candidate-refuses. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-eic/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-eic/classify.py, none unassigned): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4 withholding an unrelated answer); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative); (b) 702 value, project no, candidate yes, f2441.care no on every one (176 fixtures or generated returns, 526 partials): the project folds care into dc_qp and the reply does not; no Form 2441 is completed on those returns, so the omission reaches no amount (representation on that kind); (c) 29 candidate-unknown on returns with no care (f2441.care no), asking dc_incapable (27, e.g. classm.aqee.2 and .deepseek k0, classm.scveh.3 dep_a, stage18.blind.p15 k0), dc_under13 (stage18.mut.family_of_20 k12) or born_died (generated 100 dep_a): answers the source does not need without care expenses; (d) 1 candidate-unknown lawful (stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn all_year); (e) 54 partial records withholding an answer the reply reads and the project does not need (multiple_support 19, dc_incapable 17 with care no, lawful 3 of classm.scveh.1 dep_a, and 15 answers of classm.retirement.3 dep_b and classm.scveh.1 dep_a). Off completed returns: the reply refuses divorced_rule, other_claimant, married and multiple_support at every entry (refused returns). Project stands.

The candidate's disabled route is "dc_incapable and months > 6" for every dependent, so it drops the death-year rule BUG-0157 encoded (dependent.dc_lived_half), and its own note says it chose "the stricter entire-time rule rather than Pub. 503's more-than-half rule" although dependent.born_died and dependent.part_year_home were in the interface. p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (BUG-0157): a disabled parent, age 80, who died in 2025, months 0 as the months question instructs for a non-qualifying-child person not with you the entire time, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, dc_incapable yes, dc_paid $4,000; the project gives dc_qp yes (dependent.dc_lived_half), 2(d) $4,000 and f2441 line 11 $600; the candidate's disabled route needs months > 6 and gives dc_qp no. Other differences: (a) the joint-return route is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns)); (b) the candidate omits f2441.care, which reaches no amount, because Form 2441 sums dc_line2d only where dc_qp holds and is not completed without care (round 2, same reading). The qualifying-child-under-13 routes (i2441 p. 1, item 1) are the project's.

Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent or could claim as a dependent except: a. The disabled person had gross income of $5,200 or more, b. The disabled person filed a joint return, or c. You (or your spouse if filing jointly) could be claimed as a dependent"; i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form: "If you paid someone to care for your child or other qualifying person so you (or your spouse if filing jointly) could work or look for work in 2025, you may be able to take the credit for child and dependent care expenses"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,363 agree; 1,332 value, 779 candidate-unknown, 295 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses, 4 project-unknown. (1) Every sampled value is f2441.care no (classm.f4952.1.deepseek, classm.f8960.1.deepseek, classm.g28.1.deepseek, classm.sd.1.deepseek dep_c, completed): the candidate drops the care condition. No amount reaches Form 2441 without care (its lines are guarded by f2441.care), so the value itself is representation, as ruled in round 2; its effect on the line 2(c) box is ruled there. (2) The candidate-unknown ask dc_incapable of every entry with no care (classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3), and born_died, placed and part_year_home for a disabled child with 3 months (classm.f8962.4.deepseek dep_b): the placement route is head-of-household text (i1040gi p. 15), not Pub. 503's, which names birth or death only; model error. (3) The candidate-refuses inherit its dependent.claimed (multiple_support on a qualifying child, classm.s3.4.deepseek; other_claimant and divorced_rule on refused returns). (4) Its non-dependent route (would be a dependent but for income, joint return or being claimable) is refused by the project through f2441.nondependent (cited screen): scope. The project-refuses (stage15.refuse.dependent.dc_no_tin) is the cited claimed_no_tin screen; the project-unknown are partials withholding tin. Project stands.

The returned h_dc_child uses dc_under13 for every age. The interview asks that timing input only for the age13 boundary; younger children qualify from age without that answer. The project also retains the care-screen/claimed prerequisites. The model notes its caller assumptions, but its exported predicate is incomplete; its valid types do not resolve this source/interface defect.

Ten passing child cases are not whole-form qualification.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope/representation in the active supported dependent-care domain; i2441 (2025) p.1 gives the under13 and disabled-person alternatives. The corrected reply derives child age boundaries and uses the timing input only when age alone cannot decide; it passes all ten corrected source-based partial-input cases. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; numeric count literals in the returned h_lived_half (6) and the household-year test (12) omit type:Count. Untyped numbers are money cents in the declared IR, so comparing them with Count months yields unknown; the typed project comparison yields a Boolean. This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. Both read the household answer `f2441.care` (the second's note), the dependency tests, and the two routes of i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s): "A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent. If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13" and "Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent". The second asks `dependent.dc_under13` of every qualifying child; the project derives it from the age (under 13 at the end of 2025 is under 13 all year, 14 or over never under 13) and asks it only at 13. It also omits `sa.dependent`, refused in scope. Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you), and `dc_under13` answered consistently with the age: the only differences are the dependency-test differences ruled on dependent.odc_person (`sibling_descendant` living with you less than all year, `other` living with you all year), where the project follows i1040gi p. 19, Step 4. No change.

After normalizing nesting, the only difference from the project is that the candidate replaces "sa.dependent is no" by "f1040.status is mfj or sa.dependent is no". The candidate follows the source, i1040gi p. 18, Step 2: "3. Are you filing a joint return for 2025? Yes. You can claim this child as a dependent", asked before question 4 ("Could you be claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return?"); i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, question 4 is the same for a qualifying relative. The project tests sa.dependent alone, but the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns). Latent only: lifting the sa.dependent screen needs Step 2 question 3 and Step 4 question 4 in qc_dependent and qr_dependent. The Test 1 conditions (parent, claimed, parent_home_paid; i1040gi p. 14, Test 1) are the project's.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Test 1 (i1040gi p. 14): 'You paid over half the cost of keeping up a home that was the main home for all of 2025 of your parent whom you can claim as a dependent ... Your parent didn't have to live with you.' The project tests the parent value, the dependent line (now carrying the TIN refusal) and dependent.parent_home_paid; the second adds a residence test ('does not live with you', read as not more than half of 2025) that the text does not impose; a parent who did live with you also qualifies under Test 2, so the head of household result is the same.

They differ only when that question is answered yes for a parent who lives with you; such a dependent parent qualifies the filer through Test 2, item 1 (hoh_test2 admits a claimed parent who lived with you more than half the year), so head of household eligibility is the same. Sampling (40,000 inputs, refusal triggers false) finds no other difference. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Test 1 (i1040gi p. 14): 'You paid over half the cost of keeping up a home that was the main home for all of 2025 of your parent whom you can claim as a dependent ... Your parent didn't have to live with you.' The project tests the parent value, the dependent line (now carrying the TIN refusal) and dependent.parent_home_paid; the second adds a residence test ('does not live with you', read as not more than half of 2025) that the text does not impose; a parent who did live with you also qualifies under Test 2, so the head of household result is the same.

As in the earlier review, the second transcription adds 'did not live with you more than half the year' to Test 1; i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 1: "Your parent didn't have to live with you." Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you) (Stage 15 re-run): every difference is a parent who lived with you more than half the year, supported by you, with `dependent.parent_home_paid` answered yes; such a parent qualifies the filer through Test 2, item 1 ("Any person whom you can claim as a dependent"; hoh_test2 admits them), so head of household eligibility is the same. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 14, Test 2 (a qualifying person who lived with you more than half the year; your qualifying child or a qualifying relative related as listed; item 2, your unmarried qualifying child who isn't your dependent); p501 p. 9, Death or birth; i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative’s support, special rules may apply"; i1040gi p. 17, Step 1 (a qualifying child is tested on relationship, age, own support, joint return and residency; no support test of yours). The per-person test (residency, then a dependent qualifying child or listed relative, or an unmarried qualifying child who is not your dependent) is the project's, and its note leaves the cost of the home to household.home_cost, as the project does (BUG-0258 rewords that question only). It inherits its dependent.claimed. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.json`; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,487 partial records; 7,463 comparisons): 6,861 of 7,463 agree; 317 project-refuses, 117 candidate-refuses, 100 project-unknown, 68 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 83 candidate-refuses, 23 candidate-unknown, 3 project-unknown. Every completed-return difference was enumerated with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/dependent.full.json, causes assigned by /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-household/classify.py, none unassigned; the uncapped rerun reproduces the recorded counts exactly): (a) 83 candidate-refuses: dependent.multiple_support refused on a qualifying child, all classm.s3.4 dep_a (a child aged 2, 12 months, multiple_support yes; the fixtures classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek and 81 partial records of classm.s3.4); the project claims the child (multiple support is refused only on dependent.qualifying_relative); (b) 3 candidate-unknown dependent.born_died: the reply's dependent.h_residency asks it of every person with months under 7, but dependent.months already folds in the birth, death and placement exception ("For a person born, died, adopted or placed with you in 2025 who meets the other conditions to be your qualifying child, enter 12 if your home was their home for more than half the time they were alive or with you"; i1040gi p. 21, Exception to time lived with you), so the interview never asks it there (classm.f8960.2 and .deepseek dep_a, audit.dependent.listed_not_dependent_no_tin child); an answer the source does not need; (c) 20 partial records withholding an answer the reply needs (19 multiple_support, 1 citizen); (d) 3 project-unknown partial records of classm.scveh.1 dep_a withholding divorced_rule, married or other_claimant. Project stands.

The candidate now has the part-year route (born_died or placed, and part_year_home), and its exclusion of household_member, sibling_descendant and other agrees with the project on every sampled record. Every difference comes from its dependent.claimed: the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records of classm.f2441.1.deepseek and classm.f2441.5.deepseek): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply". The candidate requires months > 6 for every Test 2 person and has no part-year route: it never reads dependent.born_died, dependent.placed or dependent.part_year_home, which the published interface offered. The source gives a relative other than a qualifying child the part-year rule: i1040gi p. 15: "If the person is your qualifying child, the child must have lived with you for more than half the part of the year the child was alive. If the person is anyone else, see Pub. 501. Similarly, if you adopted the person ... the person is considered to have lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your main home was this person's main home for more than half the time since the person was adopted or placed with you in 2025"; p501 p. 9, Death or birth: "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage8.hoh.adopted_part_year (BUG-0158): an adult child adopted in 2025, a qualifying relative with months 0 and part_year_home yes, placed yes; the project gives hoh_test2 yes (line 12e $23,625 head of household), the candidate gives no because it needs months > 6; the stage8 death-year parent case (born_died yes, part_year_home yes) is the same. Other differences: (a) the joint-return route on sa.dependent is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference (round-2 triage of the same reading found 2 differences, both on refused returns)); (b) the candidate drops "dependent.married is no" on the qualifying-child route, which is representation because dependent.qualifying_child refuses on dependent.married (Married person, i1040gi p. 18), so no computed return has a married qualifying child.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both count a dependent who lived with you more than half the year, leaving out one who is your dependent only because they lived with you all year, and an unmarried qualifying child (i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 2, items 1, 1b and 2); items 1a, 1c, 3 and 4 are refused on both sides (the project through dependent.divorced_rule, dependent.multiple_support and dependent.married on the lines this one reads), and the project now carries the TIN refusal (dependent.claimed_no_tin; p. 22, 'You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)'). The second writes the same exclusions in its own structure.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; numeric count literals in the returned h_lived_half (6) and the household-year test (12) omit type:Count. Untyped numbers are money cents in the declared IR, so comparing them with Count months yields unknown; the typed project comparison yields a Boolean. This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), refused in scope (it refuses the standard deduction); the rule for children of divorced or separated parents is refused on the entry (`dependent.divorced_rule`). Stage 15 re-run: both sides now count a filer or spouse who has applied for an ITIN (`person.itin_applied`) in the joint-return identification test (household.all_tin). Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): the only differences come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative whatever the time lived with you, and from its excluding `other` living with you all year. i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, lists "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" (which is `sibling`; the enum defines `sibling_descendant` as any other descendant of a sibling) and "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household", which admits `other` living with you all year and admits `sibling_descendant` only on that footing, as the project does. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both count a dependent who lived with you more than half the year, leaving out one who is your dependent only because they lived with you all year, and an unmarried qualifying child (i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 2, items 1, 1b and 2); items 1a, 1c, 3 and 4 are refused on both sides (the project through dependent.divorced_rule, dependent.multiple_support and dependent.married on the lines this one reads), and the project now carries the TIN refusal (dependent.claimed_no_tin; p. 22, 'You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)'). The second writes the same exclusions in its own structure.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted complete facts; i1040gi (2025) pp.17-19 gives the same dependency, CTC/ODC identification, income/support and relationship requirements. The corrected reply now includes lawful all-year other/sibling_descendant relationships. Count months >=7 versus >6 is equivalent over whole-number inputs, and the age predicate is factored differently without changing its admitted result. Its joint-return/claimable-filer alternative extends a refused sa.dependent=true regime; that excluded regime is not admitted by this ruling. No whole-form qualification is inferred.
